content.title: About
content.content: Celery juice is obtained by pressing fresh celery stalks (Apium graveolens). It has a light green color, a mild aroma, and a slightly salty taste. The juice is often consumed fresh as a tonic drink or used in culinary and detox programs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Celery belongs to the Apiaceae family and is grown in temperate climates.
Celery juice is more than 90 % water, making it an excellent hydrating beverage.
Ancient cultures used celery as a medicinal plant to aid digestion.
Celery can reduce body odor thanks to its volatile compounds.
The juice is a common ingredient in green smoothies and detox cocktails.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Celery juice contains vitamin C, quercetin, and other polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: Its high water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids in blood pressure regulation and heart function.

items.title: Provides sodium and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are important for nerve and muscle function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Phytonutrients and fiber in the juice promote normal bowel movements.

items.title: Celery allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions such as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The juice can contain notable amounts of sodium, which should be considered by people with hypertension.

items.title: Possible drug interactions
items.content: Celery may enhance the effects of certain anticoagulants; consult a doctor if you take such medications.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink celery juice freshly prepared, chilled or diluted with water. It can be added to smoothies, cocktails, soups, and sauces. A typical serving is 100–250 ml per day.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in an airtight bottle in the refrigerator for up to 3–5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portions.
